The brief

It is Thursday, June 30, 2022. You are the managing partner of a seed fund. The fund is hypothetical; the market is not.

Your fund (hypothetical parameters; the ranges come from the two real firms in the notes): - Fund I: $150M, 2021 vintage, ~45% of investable capital called. Planned 3-year investment period, ending mid-2024. - Checks and ownership: first checks of $1.5–3.5M for 10–15% ownership. Reserves at about 1:1, so roughly half of each fund is held back for follow-ons. - Portfolio: about 18 companies. Most raised at 2021 prices, and roughly a third will need a Series A within 18 months. - LPs: two endowments, a fund-of-funds, a corporate, and about 30 family offices and individuals. - Plan of record: launch Fund II in mid-2023, targeting $200M.

What you can see today (verify every figure; none of it should be taken from this brief on trust): - Rates: the Fed has hiked three times since March. Effective fed funds is ~1.2% at quarter-end, and core PCE inflation is running ~4–5% above it. The policy rate is still well below inflation. - The yield curve: 10y minus 2y is +0.06, a few basis points from inverting. - Public markets: growth stocks have repriced sharply and the IPO window has been shut for months. VIX averaged ~27 in the quarter. - Credit and banks: the Baa spread is ~2.1, not alarming. Banks are still net easing C&I lending standards (SLOOS about −1.5% to −8% across the latest readings). - The regime classifier, as of today (_ingest/regimes.py --asof 2022-06-30), reads Boom for 2022Q1 and Q2. - A peer's read: a respected NYC seed GP says public markets and growth investors have repriced, but seed "hasn't gotten the memo." He expects seed pricing to reset within about six months. (primary venture partners insights §8, mid-2022 interview.)

The tension. The lagging gauges say Boom. The leading ones (hikes, curve, the dead IPO window, growth-stage repricing) say the money is about to get more expensive and stop coming back. Your Fund II plan assumes LPs who are still writing checks in mid-2023.

The decision: pick one of three plans, and state what's the single thing that, if wrong, sinks it:

  1. Hold: keep Fund I's 3-year deployment pace and the mid-2023 Fund II launch.
  2. Brace: slow Fund I to a 4–5 year pace, raise reserves for the portfolio, and keep the Fund II date.
  3. Run for the window: launch Fund II now (Q3 2022) at a smaller target to close before LPs freeze, and slow Fund I.

(A fourth plan is allowed if you can defend it.)

Pull the real data (as of the decision date — no hindsight)

python3 _ingest/regimes.py --asof 2022-06-30 --since 2000     # regime history using only data to that date

FRED series (stop reading at 2022-06-30): FEDFUNDS, T10Y2Y, T10Y3M, BAA10Y, DRTSCILM (SLOOS), NFCI, VIXCLS, PCEPILFE. Name the indicator you trust most and say why it beats the others for this decision.

Hindsight firewall

Allowed before the memo: the concept sections of the WSS notes: - wss rates macro: curve, FOMC, financial conditions - wss private markets wealth: the distribution clock, denominator effect, LP behavior - wss credit distressed - wss capital markets ma: IPO window - harlem capital vc insights: fund math - primary venture partners insights §§2–3: ownership, reserves, the opportunity fund

Not until after the memo: wss scenario map (its data section narrates 2022–23), apply wss to venture, and case-05-outcome.md. Several WSS notes also mention 2023–26 events in passing. If you hit one, note it in the memo, so the red team can discount for leakage.

Canon to bring to bear

canon-klarman-margin-of-safety (dry powder; don't need the good case) · canon-taleb-antifragile (who is the forced seller when funding is pulled) · canon-tetlock-superforecasting (base rates and calibrated updating) · canon-mauboussin-success-equation (vintage luck vs. skill in fund returns)

Four, deliberately. The case is built to test whether you use base rates (how often does a hiking cycle with a flattening curve end in a credit crunch?) rather than narrate.

Your deliverable

Full memo (one page, spec in README.md), written to your LP advisory committee: - BLUF: which plan. - The crux: what you believe about the next 18 months that your plan depends on. - Three reasons, each with a real, dated figure. - The fatal risk and its mitigation. - The ask: what you need from LPs (e.g. an extension of the investment period, approval to reallocate reserves).

Attach three forecasts, each with a probability, resolving by 2023-12-31: 1. Market: the quarterly regime per regimes.py (Boom / Lender's market / Drought / Shock) will be ______ in 2023Q2. (p = __%) 2. Bank credit: SLOOS net tightening (DRTSCILM) will exceed 30% in at least one quarter of 2023. (p = __%) 3. Your own: under your plan, Fund II reaches a first close of at least ___% of target by ______. (p = __%) This one is about seed fundraising in general.
